explanation: erdosproblems.com/542: Schinzel and Szekeres 'further proved that, for any ε > 0, there is such a sequence for which the sum is > 1 − ε'. The Lean version asks, for all ε, δ > 0, for n and lcm-free A ∌ 1 with |uncovered| ≤ δn and Σ 1/a > 1 − ε, i.e. the docstring's combined 'o(n) uncovered and sum > 1 − ε'. This is slightly stronger than the page's sentence taken alone, but it follows from the page's other recorded result (examples with ≤ n/(log n)^c uncovered for infinitely many n), since in an lcm-free set multiples of distinct elements are disjoint, so uncovered ≥ n(1 − Σ 1/a) forces Σ 1/a ≥ 1 − (log n)^{−c}. So the statement is true and represents the Schinzel–Szekeres construction. Faithful.
